title: React Native: Screen and controls
lead: Change sources and Player settings in an iOS or Android development build, then check playback, subtitles, API results and events.

blocks.text: The Settings, APIs, Code and More tabs sit below Source and Theme. In Settings, select a group and field to open its editor. Unapplied changes marks a pending draft; Up to date means it matches the current configuration. Apply configuration and Reset draft remain outside the scrolling editor.

blocks.title: Display language
blocks.text: Use the language controls above the selectors to switch between English and Japanese. In compact layouts or with larger text, use More. Switching retains applied settings and drafts. Screenshots on this page use English; SDK names, code and returned data keep their original spelling.

blocks.title: Before opening the screen
blocks.text: Use the generated Expo development build. Expo Go lacks the required native Player modules. Both the iOS bundle identifier and Android package name are com.playerlab.reactnative; authorize this ID on the Player license for the target platform. Follow the links below to generate the host or refresh its configuration.

items.label: Generate and run the Expo development host
Integrate the Expo host and Player

blocks.text: Choose a source and apply a change

blocks.caption: The iOS settings workspace. Select a source property directly; Apply configuration and Reset draft remain outside the editor.
The Android settings workspace uses the same categories and direct property selector, including external WebVTT subtitle inputs.

items: Select a VOD sample under Source and play it with the Player UI. iOS offers HLS and progressive MP4; Android also offers DASH.
In Settings, select Source and the field to edit. Use an HTTP or HTTPS URL and match Source type to the media. Title, poster and start position are optional. Record values you will need to restore.

Keep the URL unchanged, enter 5 in Start offset (seconds), and select Start in Start offset reference. Apply configuration, then play with the Player UI if autoplay is off. Check SourceLoaded in More and the actual starting position.
Open Code to inspect the applied values. Even a source-only form change recreates the Player. Invalid inputs or an unchanged configuration leave the current Player in place.
Reset draft discards pending edits. To undo an applied change, enter the previous value and Apply. Selecting a source sample replaces source fields and retains Player settings.

rows: Compare autoplay and initial mute after Apply. These switches do not call play or mute on the current session.
Check the position after Apply. Start refers to the beginning of the media or live window; End refers to its end or the live edge.
Compare buffering and playback after Apply. Clear the field to use the platform default. This value does not specify startup time.
Enter a whole number without units or commas and compare selected quality on a multi-quality source. Clear the field to remove the cap.

blocks.text: Enter times as finite decimal seconds. A buffer value of 0 means automatic selection on iOS; use a positive value or blank on Android. Initially autoplay and startup mute are off, and buffer and bitrate fields are blank. The implementation guide lists numeric limits, SDK defaults and configuration paths.
Compare playback, tracks and Player UI

blocks.caption: The iOS build after enabling an external subtitle with Player.setSubtitleTrack in APIs. A timed cue is visible over the native video.
The Android build with the selected external subtitle displayed. The subtitle is enabled through the Player’s track selection, not by Mark as default alone.

items: Try play, pause and seek in the Player UI. Switch audio tracks on a source with alternate audio. More contains the live rewind controls and status. Allow DVR toggles the app’s rewind helper.
Select Default, Sports, Live (DVR) or Cinema under Theme. A theme change recreates the Player and loads the applied source. Compare the controls and UI settings in Code using the same source.
In Settings → Source, enter an external WebVTT subtitle URL, label and language. Match cue times to the media and use a language tag such as en-US.
After Apply, select the label in the Player’s subtitle menu and play through a cue. Mark as default sets metadata; it does not enable display by itself.
To remove the subtitle, clear its URL and Apply. Its label and language are also cleared. Finish by restoring the previous theme and any changed Player settings.

blocks.title: Scrolling inside the Android Player menu
blocks.text: Swipe inside the video to scroll a Player menu, or inside Settings to scroll an editor. You do not need to scroll the whole screen, including the video, to select settings or APIs.

items.label: Player UI implementation and bundled themes

blocks.caption: Code in the iOS build displays wrapped applied configuration and Copy code. Pending draft edits are excluded.

items: After Apply, open Code to inspect Player, source and UI settings. Save the output before changing another field to compare the difference.
Editing a value and switching to Code without applying leaves the output unchanged. Reset draft discards only pending edits.
Use Copy code to copy the output. Licenses appear as placeholders; keep those placeholders when sharing.
The output contains applied settings supplied by the app, not every internal SDK default. See the implementation guide for the usePlayer and PlayerView connections.

blocks.text: Edit additional SDK settings and lists
SDK overrides edits settings outside the basic form; Subtitles and ads edits arrays. These editors use fields exposed by the installed React Native wrapper.

items: Select SDK overrides in Settings. Search for a path such as SourceConfig.description and choose Set this API value. Record its current value and whether an override was already enabled.
Follow the displayed type. Lists use one item per line; maps use unique name=value pairs; enums use SDK choices. UI settings also provides the UI-related fields.

In Subtitles and ads, select the array, then Edit this list and Add list item. Subtitles need URL, label, language and format; ads need position and advertising sources. Source and offline subtitle lists are separate.

After Apply, compare Code with playback, menus or events. Overrides take precedence over basic fields. Removing one restores the basic field or SDK default; applying an enabled empty list clears the array.

items.label: Array, advertising and override mappings and prerequisites

blocks.text: Try callbacks and native UI handlers

blocks.caption: An explicitly enabled network callback body on iOS. The function changes volume and returns the request.

items: In Settings → JavaScript callbacks, search for PlayerConfig.networkConfig.preprocessHttpRequest and select Edit this callback. Check its arguments and required return type.
Enter the function body, enable Allow edited JavaScript execution and Apply. The default body returns the request. When the matching request occurs, inspect the event log and the state you changed.
For fullscreen or custom messages, follow the type and factory contract shown by the editor. The implementation guide explains execution timing and return requirements.

Remove the callback and Apply when finished. Restore any Player state changed by its body, or recreate the Player from applied settings. JavaScript runs inside the app without a sandbox; allow only trusted code.

blocks.text: Run commands and inspect state and events

blocks.caption: The Android APIs workspace after running Player.getCurrentTime, showing the submitted call and returned value.

items: Open APIs, choose Operations in API view, then find Player.getCurrentTime in API operation. Choose a time mode and select Run selected API. Executed call displays the submitted SDK code; Result displays its returned value. API error marks a failed call or invalid input. Read again during playback and compare the position, in seconds, with the picture.

Try Player.pause, then choose Player.isPaused in State and select Read state. Restore playback with Player.play in Operations. For a call without a return value, use the resulting state and matching events to check its effect.
Events displays recent SDK payload summaries. Pause event log stops recording; resume it to collect new events. Clear API event log removes the displayed comparison history.

After destroying the Player or to restore applied settings, open API help and select Recreate player after API experiments. Query resource and track identifiers again from the replacement Player or source.

blocks.caption: The iOS event log shows recent SDK events and their payloads. Event recording and API state queries are separate ways to inspect the same session.

blocks.text: You can search by a method name such as play. An exact match at the end of an API name comes first, so Player.play leads those results; other matches remain below it.

Some listed operations are platform-specific. In wrapper 1.29, Player.setVideoQuality and auto work on Android; iOS warns and makes no selection. On iOS, compare Maximum bitrate with the selected quality. Leave the Player.setSubtitleTrack input blank to disable subtitles.

Offline operations affect the selected content identifier. Check onCompleted before loading the stored media with Player.loadOfflineContent. Recreating the Player does not clear storage, so confirm the target before cancellation, deletion or license operations. See the implementation guide for initialization and download prerequisites.

items.label: Track, native integration and offline prerequisites

blocks.caption: The Android Cast startup panel after a full restart: savedOptions and startupOptions agree, nativeInitialized is true and pendingRestart is false. This does not show receiver playback.

items: In Settings → SDK overrides, set BitmovinCastManagerOptions.applicationId and messageNamespace. Blank uses the default receiver and namespace. Record the values to restore.

Under Cast startup settings, select Save Cast options for next launch, then fully close and reopen the app. Saving is independent of Apply. A JavaScript reload or Player recreation does not apply these options.
Read native Cast startup state and compare savedOptions, startupOptions, nativeInitialized and pendingRestart. Check startup application separately from receiver discovery, connection and playback.

Try discovery, connection and playback with a compatible receiver on the same network. To restore options, save the original values and fully restart again. The implementation guide explains platform-specific state reporting and initialization.
